clue.text: Republican in seemingly unpopulated county?

indicators.note: the Republican is placed in the middle of the phrase that follows it

parts.note: a place that seems empty has 'no folk', no people

explanation.surface: A political question about whether a sparsely settled rural area really has any Republican voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. Norfolk is a rural county in eastern England, often joked about as empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Norfolk is an English county in East Anglia, an example of the category.

clue.text: Cooked beans go in food container

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are doctored or fiddled into another order

explanation.surface: Cooked beans being tipped into a food tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges BEANS GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebag is a bag of feed hung over a horse's muzzle, a container for fodder.

clue.text: Taxi provider, needing lift, first to solve puzzle

indicators.note: in a down entry a lift raises the word, so it reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: Uber is a ride-hailing company providing taxi rides

indicators.note: first to picks only the opening letter of solve

explanation.surface: A taxi firm that needs to give someone a lift before solving a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing lift' turns UBER upwards into REBU; 'first to' takes S from 'solve'. 'Lift' looks like a ride, which suits the taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle in which pictures or symbols stand for words or syllables.

clue.text: Girl in green

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a girl's name and the name of a muted greenish shade.

clue.text: King on Hampshire river where trout prepared?

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
the Itchen is a famous trout river in Hampshire

explanation.surface: A king fishing on a Hampshire river, where trout are caught.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county in southern England; the Itchen flows through Winchester and Southampton. The trout looks freshly caught, but the definition is where it is cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen is the room where food such as fish is prepared and cooked.

clue.text: Rich sort of cake popular — great for starter

parts.note: a Swiss roll is a sort of cake
in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so only the opening letter of great is used

explanation.surface: A dessert menu praising a rich, popular cake as a great opening course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starter' takes G, the first letter of 'great'. 'Rolling' means rich, as in the phrase 'rolling in it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wealthy is said to be rolling in money, an informal idiom for being very well off.

clue.text: Reportedly studied beloved animal

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are taken as they are heard, not spelt

parts.note: studied is read, and beloved is dear

explanation.surface: Someone said to have read about a much-loved animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The red deer is a large deer species of Europe and Asia, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Cut a liver out — it's financially rewarding

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Organ harvesting described as a lucrative business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CUT A LIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucrative means producing a great deal of profit, money-making.

clue.text: Nervous Shakespeare wife missing some banter?

indicators.note: missing means the abbreviation for wife is lost from the poet's name

parts.note: William Shakespeare is known as Will
a means some, one or any, as in 'a few'
to tease is to banter, mock playfully

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's anxious wife being left out of the witty exchanges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops W from WILL to leave ILL. 'Shakespeare wife' looks like Anne Hathaway, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ill at ease is uncomfortable and anxious, an idiom for being nervous.

clue.text: Try to catch rook that hurt amusing brother

indicators.note: to catch means the trial word wraps around the bird and the cry

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt
R is the chess abbreviation for rook
ouch is what you say when something hurts

explanation.surface: Someone trying to catch a rook and getting a painful peck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch' is the container signal; 'that hurt' supplies the exclamation itself. Groucho Marx was one of the Marx Brothers comedy team.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho was the wisecracking Marx Brother, a comic, so he is an amusing sibling.

clue.text: Gave in and proposed

definitions.meaning: to yield or surrender to another's will
put forward an idea or document for consideration

explanation.definitionFit: The verb has two senses: yielding to authority, and presenting something for judgement or approval.

clue.text: Boss carries doubly large instrument

indicators.note: the boss holds the doubled letter within, as if carrying it

parts.note: CEO, chief executive officer, is the boss of a company

indicators.note: doubly says the letter for large is written twice

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A company chief lugging around an especially big musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' writes the letter for large twice, and 'carries' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a bowed string instrument of the violin family, an example of the category.

clue.text: Able regularly to visit church and pray

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of Able, here the second and fourth

parts.note: to see someone is to visit them, as in seeing a doctor

explanation.surface: Advice that anyone able should go to church regularly and say their prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks B and E from 'Able'; 'Able regularly' reads like a pious habit but is pure mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to beg or implore earnestly, a near synonym of praying in its sense of entreating.

clue.text: Bouncy castle collapsed, engulfing one

indicators.note: engulfing means the rearranged letters swallow up the numeral within them
a collapsed structure falls apart, so the letters of castle are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A children's bouncy castle deflating and swallowing a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' rearranges CASTLE into ELASTC, and 'engulfing' puts I inside it. 'Bouncy castle' looks like one phrase, but 'Bouncy' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elastic springs back into shape, so it is springy or resilient.

clue.text: Many barrels among this smuggler's contraband?

definitions.text: Many barrels among this smuggler's contraband?

parts.words: Many barrels among this smuggler's contraband?
parts.note: barrels suggests casks of brandy, but they are the barrels of illegally traded firearms

explanation.walkthrough: Barrels sound like casks of rum or brandy, the classic smuggled goods, but here they are the barrels of rifles.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunrunner smuggles weapons, and guns have barrels, so the contraband contains many barrels.

clue.text: Leg in cast — chap being careless

indicators.note: cast suggests the letters are thrown and reshaped into a new form

parts.note: gent, short for gentleman, means a chap

explanation.surface: A man with his leg in plaster, having been careless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges LEG IN into NEGLI. 'Cast' looks like a plaster cast for the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent means failing to take proper care, a synonym for careless.

clue.text: Ran about in frenzy circling Lima's capital

indicators.note: circling means the rearranged letters go round the letter for Lima
in frenzy means the letters of ran about are wildly mixed up

parts.note: Lima is the radio alphabet code word for L

explanation.surface: Someone dashing about frantically around Lima, the Peruvian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in frenzy' rearranges RAN ABOUT, and 'circling' puts L inside. 'Lima's capital' looks like a first letter, but Lima is the radio code for L and 'capital' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulan Bator is the capital city of Mongolia, an example of a capital.

clue.text: Union member seen in Almeida Hotel

indicators.note: the letters can be seen inside the words Almeida Hotel, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A trade union delegate spotted staying at a hotel called the Almeida.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union member' suggests a trade unionist, but the union is the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty states making up the federal union of the USA.

clue.text: Old woman after plague offers opinion

indicators.note: the old woman comes after the plague in the answer

parts.note: to dog someone is to plague or harass them
ma is an informal word for mother, one's old woman

explanation.surface: An elderly woman, recovered from a plague, holds forth with her views.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogma is a firmly held belief or doctrine, an opinion laid down as beyond dispute.

clue.text: Alien concealed in exhaust? Leave car

indicators.note: the alien is hidden inside the word for exhaust

parts.note: to drain is to exhaust or use up
ET is the film alien, the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: An alien hiding in a car's exhaust pipe, then told to get out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhaust' looks like a car part, but it is a verb meaning drain. 'Car' is a railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: To detrain is to get off a train, leaving the railway carriage.

clue.text: English daisy for example: good seasonal item

parts.note: the aster is a flower of the daisy family, so a daisy of sorts

explanation.surface: A gardening note: the English daisy is a good flower to grow for the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English daisy' reads as one flower name, but English and daisy are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate egg given at Easter is an item tied to that particular season of the year.

clue.text: Relentless outside losing vote

indicators.note: losing means the voting mark drops out of the word for outside

parts.note: external means outside
X is the mark made on a ballot paper to vote

explanation.surface: A relentless campaigner outside the hall after losing the vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes X out of EXTERNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal never ends or lets up, so it is unceasing or relentless.

clue.text: Like controversial verses thus written about a function

indicators.note: about means the editorial word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: sic is Latin for 'thus', used to show a quotation is written exactly so
tan, short for tangent, is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A note on the controversial verses, written about how a function works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. The controversial verses are Salman Rushdie's novel The Satanic Verses.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushdie's novel The Satanic Verses provoked a fatwa, so the adjective describes those controversial verses.

clue.text: Setter for example served up old language

indicators.note: in a down entry served up means the abbreviation is sent upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: Latin is the language of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A crossword setter dishing up an old language in clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns EG into GE. 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but it is something that makes a jelly set.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatin is used to make jellies and desserts firm, so it is a setting agent.

clue.text: Tangled belt trapping him in sewer's cover

indicators.note: the jumbled letters close around him, trapping the word inside
tangled means the letters of belt are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man caught in a knotted belt while in a sewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tangled' rearranges the belt's letters and 'trapping' is the container signal. 'Sewer' looks like a drain but means one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: A thimble is a small cap worn on the finger to protect it when a person stitches.

clue.text: Speaker's expression, crude perhaps, brings disorder

indicators.note: a speaker says the word, so it is what it sounds like that counts

parts.note: a term is a word or expression
crude is one kind of oil, unrefined petroleum

explanation.surface: A public speaker's crude remark causes chaos in the hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker's' tells you TERM is heard, giving TURM. 'Crude' looks like an adjective for the remark but is a noun: crude oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmoil is a state of great confusion or upheaval, a synonym for disorder.

clue.text: Material in drawer Conservative ignored

indicators.note: ignored means the abbreviation for Conservative is left out

parts.note: a crayon draws, so it is a drawer

explanation.surface: Fabric found in a drawer that a Tory overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' drops C from CRAYON. 'Drawer' looks like furniture but means something that draws.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a synthetic textile made from cellulose, a kind of fabric or cloth.

clue.text: Damaged layer — Australia has one

parts.note: Oz is an informal name for Australia
taken as written

explanation.surface: Australia has a damaged layer of the atmosphere above it, the famous hole.
explanation.walkthrough: The ozone layer, damaged by CFCs, has a notorious hole over the Antarctic near Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The ozone layer in the stratosphere was thinned by pollutant gases, so it is the layer known for damage.

clue.text: Expert from A-section?

parts.note: DEPT is the abbreviation for department, a section of an organisation

explanation.surface: Asking whether a specialist comes from the top section, the A-section.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept is a highly skilled person, a master or authority in some field.

clue.text: Got any bananas to add to bread and butter?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are added after the bread

parts.note: nan (naan) is Indian flatbread

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters of got any are scrambled

explanation.surface: A shopper asks for bananas to go with bread and butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' rearranges GOT ANY into NYGOAT. 'Bread and butter' looks like one phrase, but 'butter' is the definition: one that butts.
explanation.definitionFit: A female goat butts with its head, so it is jokingly a butter, one who butts.

clue.text: Unrefined person sure to succeed

definitions.meaning: in a raw state, not processed
someone with a born talent, certain to do well

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes things in their raw state, and as a noun names someone with a born gift.

clue.text: Firm showing interest

definitions.meaning: a matter of care or involvement, or a stake in something

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means both a business enterprise and a matter that troubles or involves someone.
